title: J. K. Simmons
wiki_lead:
Jonathan Kimble Simmons (born January 9, 1955) is an American actor. Considered among the most established and enduring character actors of his generation, he has amassed over 200 screen and stage credits since his 1986 debut. He played Terence Fletcher, an abusive jazz instructor, in Damien Chazelle's Whiplash (2013) and Whiplash (2014), winning the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor for the latter performance, and received a second nomination for portraying William Frawley in Aaron Sorkin's Being the Ricardos (2021). His other various accolades include a British Academy Film Award, a Golden Globe Award, and a Screen Actors Guild Award. 
Simmons achieved international fame with his role as J. Jonah Jameson in Sam Raimi's Spider-Man trilogy (2002–2007), a role he reprised in various Marvel media unrelated to the Raimi trilogy, including multiple animated titles and the Marvel Cinematic Universe films. He has appeared in numerous supporting roles in films such as The Cider House Rules (1999), Thank You for Smoking (2005), Juno (2007), Burn After Reading (2008), Up in the Air (2009), Jennifer's Body (2009), Terminator Genisys (2015), Patriots Day (2016), La La Land (2016), Justice League (2017), Palm Springs (2020), and Juror No. 2 (2024). He played two different interpretations of Santa Claus in Klaus (2019) and Red One (2024).
On television, he rose to prominence for playing white supremacist prisoner Vernon Schillinger on the HBO series Oz (1997–2003), the recurring role of Dr. Emil Skoda on the NBC series Law & Order (1997–2010), Assistant Police Chief Will Pope on the TNT series The Closer (2005–2012), and Howard Silk in the Starz series Counterpart (2017–2019). He has also appeared in commercials for Farmers Insurance. On the Broadway stage Simmons played Captain Hook in the 1991 revival of Peter Pan and Benny Southstreet in the 1992 revival of Guys and Dolls. 
As a voice actor, he has played the Yellow M&M in commercials since 1996, Cave Johnson in the video game Portal 2 (2011), White Knight in Generator Rex (2010–2013), Tenzin in The Legend of Korra (2012–2014), Stanford "Ford" Pines in Gravity Falls (2015–2016), Kai in Kung Fu Panda 3 (2016), Mayor Leodore Lionheart in Zootopia (2016), Martin Smarty in Kim Possible (2002–2007), Nolan Grayson / Omni-Man in Invincible (2021–present) and Mortal Kombat 1 (2023), and General Ketheric Thorm in the video game Baldur's Gate 3 (2023)

Early life and education
Jonathan Kimble Simmons was born on January 9, 1955, in Grosse Pointe, Michigan, to Patricia (née Kimble; 1929–2014), an administrator, and Donald William Simmons (1928–2012), a music teacher at Parcells Middle School. One of three children, Simmons attended Ferry Elementary School in Grosse Pointe Woods. In 1965, when he was 10 years old, his family moved to Worthington, Ohio, a suburb of Columbus, Ohio. grok_lead: Jonathan Kimble Simmons (born January 9, 1955), professionally known as J. K. Simmons, is an American actor and voice artist celebrated for his commanding presence and versatility across film, television, theater, and animation, with a career spanning over four decades that includes more than 200 credits. He rose to prominence through intense character roles, such as the neo-Nazi inmate Vernon Schillinger in the HBO series Oz (1997â2003) and the bombastic newspaper editor J. Jonah Jameson in Sam Raimi's Spider-Man trilogy (2002â2007). Simmons achieved critical and commercial breakthrough with his Academy Award-winning portrayal of the abusive jazz instructor Terence Fletcher in Whiplash (2014), a performance that also earned him a Golden Globe, a Screen Actors Guild Award, and a Critics' Choice Movie Award. Born in Grosse Pointe, Michigan, to music teacher Donald William Simmons and administrator Patricia Kimble, Simmons developed an early interest in performance influenced by his father's profession. He studied music at the Ohio State University before transferring to the University of Montana, where he earned a Bachelor of Arts in music and began exploring theater. Simmons started his professional career on stage in the 1980s, appearing in regional productions and making his Broadway debut in Peter Pan (1990â1991) as Captain Hook and Mr. Darling opposite Cathy Rigby. Transitioning to screen work, he debuted in television with guest spots on shows like Miami Vice and The Equalizer, followed by recurring roles as psychiatrist Dr. Emil Skoda on Law & Order (1997â2010) and as Assistant Police Chief Will Pope on The Closer (2005â2012). In film, Simmons has excelled in supporting roles that often steal scenes, including the tobacco lobbyist BR in Thank You for Smoking (2005), the father Mac MacGuff in Juno (2007), and the CIA superior in Burn After Reading (2008). His voice work has been equally iconic, lending his gravelly baritone to characters such as Omni-Man in the animated series Invincible (2021âpresent), Tenzin in The Legend of Korra (2012â2014), Kai in Kung Fu Panda 3 (2016), and Mayor Lionheart in Zootopia (2016). Simmons received a second Academy Award nomination for Best Supporting Actor for his role as William Paley in Being the Ricardos (2021), and in 2025, he earned his first Primetime Emmy nomination for his comedic turn in the Roku series Die Hart. His recent projects include voicing the narrator in The Fish Thief: A Great Lakes Mystery (2025), starring in the thriller You Can't Run Forever (2024), and leading the geopolitical thriller series Embassy (TBA).
